🌎 BEYOND THE 956

RJ Mitte, the actor who grew up on screen as Walter White Jr. on AMC's Breaking Bad — and who turned his own life with cerebral palsy into a platform for disability visibility in Hollywood — has died at 34.

His representatives confirmed his death in a statement to the press. Mitte died October 12, 2026, at his home in Brownsville, Texas, in the Rio Grande Valley. Cameron County Justice of the Peace Cyndi Hinojosa confirmed the cause of death was suicide, according to USA Today. His mother, Dyna Mitte, found him at the family home.

Cast at just 14 years old for the pilot of Breaking Bad in 2007, Mitte played Walt Jr. across all five seasons of the series (2008–2013) as the son of Walter White (Bryan Cranston) and Skyler White (Anna Gunn). Born with cerebral palsy, like his character, he brought lived experience to a role that made him one of the most visible disabled actors in television history. The show earned 16 Primetime Emmy Awards across 58 nominations.

\"RJ Mitte, my sweet son on Breaking Bad has died,\" Cranston wrote on Instagram. \"Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never — ever — allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything.\" Anna Gunn called him her \"beloved\" TV son, writing that he \"lit up our lives\" and made her proud through his tireless advocacy and philanthropic work.

Beyond acting, Mitte built a career as an advocate: he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's, led the Mitte Foundation supporting scholarships and community grants, and received SAG-AFTRA's Harold Russell Award in 2014. His other screen credits included Campbell Bingham on Switched at Birth and the film Triumph.

His family held a Celebration of Life on October 16 at the Mitte Cultural District in Brownsville, where his sister Lacianne Carriere tearfully called him her \"other half\" and urged anyone who is struggling to reach out for help.

If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, emotional distress, or substance use, call or text 988 in the United States to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline — free, confidential, 24/7, with services in Spanish.

Sources: statement from RJ Mitte's representatives via spokesperson Sean Riley; PEOPLE; USA Today; Entertainment Weekly; The Associated Press.

title: Beyond the 956: RJ Mitte, 'Breaking Bad's' Walter White Jr. and disability advocate, dies at 34
